<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with vivid, well-targeted examples and disciplined use of ordinary background knowledge rather than fake sourcing. PRO's spine — harm lives in the pattern, doxxing is irreversible, choose the error you can undo — was memorably framed and landed real damage on CON's per-post remedy (the "reload mechanism" point). But CON built the cleaner decisive frame and never lost it: since posted addresses and locating details are already removable content, the motion's *marginal* reach is precisely the non-threatening amplifiers, and separating a raid from a movement there requires exactly the contextual human judgment that "immediate" deletes. CON pressed this consistently and honestly, including an explicit, defended concession that the "she works at this hospital" account goes untouched by design. CON also converted PRO's own answers into concessions: PRO's observability list was shown to match viral callouts, PRO added the unobservable "private-figure target" rider, and PRO's gloss of immediacy as "hours... against the cluster the evidence identifies" invited CON's sharpest line, "that is review." PRO's closing gotcha — that CON's own answer read context, so both rules judge context and only timing remains — was clever and the best PRO moment, but CON's reply that "she's home alone Thursdays" carries its own harm without any cluster analysis or headcount largely defused it. On weighing, PRO's reversibility asymmetry was PRO's strongest asset and was only partly neutralized by CON's "the moment closes too" answer; still, CON's demonstration that PRO's rule adds mostly the risky cases while catching little the status quo misses made the choice easier to decide. Minor execution cost to CON for repeated clipping, including a truncated closing, which is why the margin stays competitive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B2.3]/[B3.1] squeeze: after PRO ruled the workplace/spouse accountability example "outside the motion," CON asked what the motion then adds, since posted addresses are already removable — leaving PRO defending suspension only for the non-doxxing amplifiers. Compounded by CON's [B4.5] catch that PRO's own signal list matched viral callouts and required an unobservable "private-figure" rider plus evidence "identified by whom?", which reframed PRO's immediacy as concealed review.</best_rebuttal>
